 Gold, silver rates today, November 21: Gold jewellery prices fall again; why silver is falling even faster
 By Upstox News Desk 4 min read | Updated on November 21, 2026, 13:02 IST
 Preferred news source Select Upstox as your Preferred news source SUMMARY
 Gold fell ₹49 to ₹12,508 a gram and silver held at ₹175 a gram, or ₹1,75,000 a kilogram, but silver has lost 16.67% from its November 5 peak against gold's 14.34%
 Silver prices are falling faster than gold. The article looks at the reason. | Image: Shutterstock
 Gold prices declined again on Saturday, November 21, with 24 karat at ₹12,508 per gram, down ₹49 from Friday's rate , according to GoodReturns data at the time of writing. This is the sixth consecutive day of decline, a run that has taken ₹1,254 a gram off the yellow metal since November 15. Silver rate was unchanged at ₹175 a gram, or ₹1.75 lakh a kilogram.

 Gold and silver rates on November 1 and November 21, 2026; indicative prices before making charges and GST 
 The gap between the two metals has a cause that gold does not share. Silver's industrial and jewellery demand is contracting at the same time as its investment appeal is weakening. The Silver Institute expects global silver jewellery demand to decline 22% and silverware demand 17% in 2026, with US retail investment falling to its lowest level since 2010 and Indian demand forecast to drop 10% this year. 
 Higher prices and weaker rural spending in India are pushing buyers towards smaller, lighter pieces, while changing preferences in China and subdued demand in Europe and the United States are weighing on volumes.
 In the sarafa bazaar, silver is down 19% since November 5 and 61% from its record peak of ₹4.04 lakh a kilogram on January 29, 2026.
 The reasons for the slide are now well documented, and they have little to do with Indian demand.
 A stronger dollar, elevated US Treasury yields and expectations of another interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve have together made gold less attractive against bonds. The rupee's own strength has added to the pressure on domestic prices, since a firmer rupee lowers the landed cost of imported bullion.
 In a PTI report, Gaurav Garg, head of research at the investment platform Lemonn, was quoted as saying that the correction was being driven by rising US rate expectations, with the dollar holding near a 19-month high and elevated Treasury yields making non-yielding precious metals less attractive.
 Forced liquidations across markets and sticky inflation have added to the selling, according to the expert, because both have lifted yields and reinforced the dollar.
 In rupee terms the domestic fall has been severe. The 99.9% purity rate in the Delhi sarafa market crashed ₹5,200 to ₹1,29,300 per 10 gram, inclusive of all taxes, on Friday, according to the PTI report. That is a cumulative loss of ₹17,600 per 10 grams, or 12%, since November 9, when the metal stood at ₹1,46,900.
 Measured from the record ₹1.83 lakh per 10 grams in January this year, gold has lost ₹53,700, or 29.3%.
 How much you have to pay for 10-gram gold jewellery?
 Investors should note that online gold rates are indicative, excluding GST and making charges. The sarafa rate quoted by PTI is inclusive of all taxes. A jewellery piece of 10 grams of 22 karat can today cost around ₹1,14,650 for the metal, ₹13,758 of making charges at 12% and ₹3,852 for GST, taking the total to ₹1,32,260.
 Making charges can range from 5% to 18% or higher, depending on the jewellery's design.
 Lower gold and silver prices are expected to bring physical buyers back to the market, particularly for wedding shopping.
 PTI quoted Renisha Chainani, chief research officer at Augmont, as saying that purchases had risen this week as families took advantage of more attractive rates.
